pages.title: Work
pages.content:
Four pieces, signed

Bakery refit, school sports hall, housing co-op car park and lift motor room: the four pieces apprentices leave behind, each signed by the person who watched it being made.

pages.title: Apprenticeship
pages.content:
Four days on site, one day here

A twelve-week foundation term at the college, a trial week with an employer, then a three-year apprenticeship: four days on site, one day back in the workshop.

pages.title: How we judge
pages.content:
Six signed pieces a year

The board, the tray run, the gland, the test sheet, the site visit and the logbook. A year is complete when all six pieces are signed.

pages.title: Employers
pages.content:
When an employer takes a trainee on

The foundation term is complete, the first two pieces are signed, and a trial week on site has been done with a visit from our assessor on day three.

pages.title: Instructors
pages.content:
Who watches the work

Ines Varga, Rhea Lindqvist, Kofi Mensah and Paloma Iturbe sign every piece an apprentice builds.

pages.title: Fees & intakes
pages.content:
Fees and intakes

January 2027 intake starts Monday 11 January 2027; applications close Friday 27 November 2026. September 2027 intake starts Monday 6 September 2027; applications close Friday 4 June 2027. 24 places each.

pages.title: Open board Saturdays
pages.content:
Come on a Saturday

The first Saturday of each month, 09:00 to 12:00, free. Try a termination with an instructor.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
The shed in 1998

Ines Varga founded Akiha College in 1998 inside a converted brick foundry shed at Foundry Row 9, Calder Quay.

posts.title: January 2027 intake: dates and the open board
posts.excerpt: The January 2027 intake starts on Monday 11 January and applications close on Friday 27 November 2026.
posts.content:
The January 2027 intake starts on Monday 11 January 2027. Applications close on Friday 27 November 2026, and there are 24 places.

If you have never terminated a cable, come to an open board Saturday first: the first Saturday of every month, 09:00 to 12:00, free, with an instructor beside you.

posts.title: What the gland tells you
posts.excerpt: Why the instructors look at the gland first when a year-one apprentice hands over a termination.
posts.content:
A cable gland is small, and it tells an instructor almost everything. Whether the armour has been cut clean, whether the sheath is scored, whether the earth tag sits tight.

In year one we ask for the same termination again and again, until the gland seals true without being fussed at.

posts.title: A day in bay two
posts.excerpt: From boards uncovered at 07:30 to tools counted at 15:45: an ordinary day in bay two.
posts.content:
07:30 boards uncovered and isolations checked. 08:00 the day’s piece is set. 10:15 tea. 12:30 lunch.

15:45 tools counted, boards covered, and the instructor signs what was watched. 16:30 the workshop is closed.
